answer: The chime cutter bevels the stave ends, and the bevel must match the head or the cask will not seal. Chime iron barrel raiser cooper writ covers the bevelling: a writ iron barrel raisers sign after raising yard checks. The beacon is the first bevel, cut at dawn; the inlet is the last, cut before the heads go in, and the umber is the head itself, fitted tight. To fake it, a cheat must cut 59 false bevels and fit 59 false heads.
